searchText: TLDR: SETCODEFROM is just superior than SETDELEGATE as it allows to do both: Remove the delegation marker to move EOA accounts into smart accounts or back to simple EOAs. And, also, reduce significantly the tax on already-deployed code deployments which is now significantly uppriced thanks to EIP-8058 being merged in G*. The major thing to review now is: We want to enable `SETCODEFROM` as an alternative method to CREATE. (And in the EIP it's marked that `SETCODEFROM` can't be called during INITCODE. This means, we either need to modify the EIP to allow it as well as make sure all the interactions and side effects this might have are fine. Or, figure out if there are easy enough alternatives `TCREATE` for example being one of them where we could do the trick.` I think a possible solution is to make SETCODEFROM terminating, this means: - initcode either ends with SETCODEFROM/RETURN/STOP etc - SETCODEFROM(T) raises an exceptional halt if T is invalid - Don't charge ACCOUNT_WRITE costs since the account is being created in initcode, vs at runtime where we are editing an existing account ---- one issue with it not being terminating are weird cases in initcode like: ``` SETCODEFROM(T) ... RETURN(bytes) ``` also note that even if called at runtime, calling SETCODEFROM doesn't change the code in the current context, so terminating might be less ambiguous(?) Posted https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-8298-setcodefrom-code-reuse-instruction/28779/18?u=cperezz This is what <@543900561460822016> proposed yesterday. And I think this should settle it. If clients agree with the behaviour.

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content:
I think a possible solution is to make SETCODEFROM terminating, this means:

- initcode either ends with SETCODEFROM/RETURN/STOP etc
- SETCODEFROM(T) raises an exceptional halt if T is invalid
- Don't charge ACCOUNT_WRITE costs since the account is being created in initcode, vs at runtime where we are editing an existing account

----

one issue with it not being terminating are weird cases in initcode like:

```
SETCODEFROM(T)
...
RETURN(bytes)
```

also note that even if called at runtime, calling SETCODEFROM doesn't change the code in the current context, so terminating might be less ambiguous(?)
